findings.observation: A no-prompt policy that reads the drawn silhouette and drops on calm won 17 of 22 levels. Goals are now kind-specific with pictured loads and mass labels, queues are scrambled with swap allowances, two late levels contain real order traps, sea sway and wind make late drops a timing task, and the landing aid shows on windy and rocking jobs only in the drop state. A kind-matching reader now wins 10 levels at 50% or more and 1 of levels 15-22.
'The tower fell' showed when material merely ran out; a separate 'Not enough material left' reason and text now cover that case.
Goal pictures, the target ghost and the mass labels were drawn fully opaque or nearly invisible because drawLoad reset globalAlpha; they now draw at 0.22, 0.35 and 0.9 with draw tests.

A literal follower lost tries on level 19 depending on the start phase. The drop prompt now waits until the trolley has stopped for 0.7 s and a swing forecast keeps the landing on the mark for 0.6 s ahead; random-start followers lose no tries on any level at 0, 0.25 or 0.5 s lag.
A required weight on level 21 had no goal picture; every plan step now has a visible goal, asserted for all 22 levels.

openNotes: On sea levels the drop prompt is available for about 0.6-0.7 s roughly every 3.2 s, so careful play can take up to about 15 s per load.
A kind-matching reader that also trusts the drop-state landing aid wins 17 levels; the bar applies to plain reading.
Sleep can hold a block within about 0.5 px of its tipping point.
The source is about 2280 lines, over the 800-line soft ceiling; generated level data accounts for much of it.
